questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The chance to experience another university was a significant motivation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No issues. The people i worked with were great.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All crucial information was provided by colleagues. Anything else I would ask them of.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A supervisor showed me to my apartment and around the university. Helped me get situated.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: My supervisor took care of the housing. I did not really have much to do with it.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Kitchen in my apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The housing is quite good. nearby is also plenty of shops needed for day-today shopping/groceries. There should be no issues for you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The room that was provided was really in a quite good condition and not too expensive. No gripes with it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some issues with the ID and with the government registration but once again my colleagues were really helpful so it was fixed with time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
In order to do work in the university, I needed an ID for most electronic stuff. This was provided after some back and forth with their IT-help desk. It took some time but was not super difficult. 
I also needed to register my address with the government which required a meeting with an office. There were some slight language barriers, but we got through it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write mails to the university for any issues with registration. They also set up the meeting that I needed to attend to in order to register my address.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i was not enrolled in any classes as I was only doing my master thesis.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the welcome package and ask if you have any doubts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt that they had prepared a nice project and were always available when needed to discuss my work.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My only course was my project. To complete the project I needed to have prior knowledge gained on my master thesis, so I would describe the level as quite fitting

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I have not had this kind of work in Copenhagen, so it would be very difficult to describe. Having my own project with day-to-day discussions with my supervisors that shape the development is a new experience. The communication with teachers is as open and easy as it would be in Copenhagen however.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Masters thesis project and Biochemie II.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would certainly recommend future students to do their thesis at BCII. The facilities are quite decent and the people are great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: several seminars for foreign students were available over zoom.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel to the neighboring cities and look around. Many places in the old industrial areas have been repurposed for recreational purposes. Very interesting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: My travels were limited to the neighboring cities due to covid. The things mentioned above would be my recommendations

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: No issue. My colleagues were from around the world, so it was nothing I had to acclimate to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Clubs and after school activites.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No significant challenges, we were similar in that way.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openness and the urge to socialize.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Take your time to get comfortable, it could take some time. There is no harm in that.
2. Bring up any issues that you may have. It is quite likely that someone else ran into your problem and could help solve it with their experience.
3. Enjoy the opportunity.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you choose a project that interests you as it will be a large part of your life for quite some time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Slowly being able to work more and more independently and understanding the work you do.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: when working on one thing for so long, fatigue did become a factor at some point. It resolved it self, however.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I am very thankful for the opportunity to go abroad, and for this institution to help me when doing so.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
